corrections.problem: “Bimonthly” is ambiguous and may mean twice a month; the source explicitly says every two months.
corrections.action: Replaced the ambiguous frequency with the source’s explicit interval.

corrections.problem: The paraphrase narrowed the source comparison to “earlier models,” while the cited passage compares the engines with any other Suzy class.
corrections.action: Changed the comparison to match the source’s full stated scope.

corrections.problem: The claim made a definitive 3,000-ton cutoff, but the source says the limit is “something in the vicinity” of 3,000 metric tons.
Vega-origin details appear in Gosia’s narration (p0007); the Mari Swa quotation in p0008 only supports the existence of broader interstellar humanity.
corrections.action: Corrected the speaker attribution to Gosia and narrowed the assertion to her statement.

corrections.problem: The cited paragraphs omitted the actual AI-flying answer; p0022 only introduces two answers.
corrections.action: Added p0023, which explicitly says anyone can fly the ship using its AI.

corrections.problem: The claim paraphrased an answer about AI intervention but cited only the answer, omitting the specific collision-course question that sets its scope.
corrections.action: Restored the trigger condition from the question and cited both question and answer.

corrections.problem: “Sand Clock is an elite 12-fighter squadron” collapsed the source’s plural Sand Clock squadrons and separate statement that each squadron has 12 fighters.
corrections.action: Rephrased to preserve group/squadron scope and the separate fighter count.

corrections.problem: The claim attributed both memory and psychic-ability statements to Mari and generalized the latter as residing in an etheric field, but the psychic-ability quote is attributed to Swaruu of Erra and says only that it is nonphysical/not in brain or gene.
corrections.action: Narrowed the claim to Mari’s directly attributed memory statement and corrected speaker/citation.

corrections.problem: The “synchronizes” component was paraphrased from the system setup but its explicit setup passage was not cited.
corrections.action: Added the paragraph stating that the Muon system was synchronized with Temmer before remote presence.

corrections.problem: The claim names Toleka, but the source names Alcyone and Asterope.
corrections.action: Corrected the ship names to match the cited passage.

corrections.problem: “Failed against” suggests the systems were activated and ineffective; the source says they had no chance to start before the cyclone developed.
corrections.action: Restored the source’s sequence and scope.

corrections.problem: “Excluded from the council” suggests intentional exclusion; the source only says the civilizations did not participate and did not know of the meeting.
corrections.action: Removed the unsupported implication and retained the source’s wording.

corrections.problem: “Threatened reduced cooperation” contradicted Ruhr’s explicit caveat that his statement was not a threat but a consequence already in progress.
corrections.action: Rephrased the claim to preserve the source’s non-threat caveat and progressive withdrawal framing.

corrections.problem: Unsupported species-specific attribution; source generalizes to some Lyrian races and most consumers.
corrections.action: Broadened the claim to most Lyrian races and retained Anéeka’s warning about Earth synthetic meat.

corrections.problem: Cited passages omitted the substantive answer; the claim included the wrong phrasing and conflated hologram details with the phase explanation.
corrections.action: Added the exact answer passage and narrowed the statement to sunlight reflection plus superimposed details.

corrections.problem: “Battle-damaged” overstated the passage, which reports evidence of a major fight in the ship’s interior; investigation is described as delayed by Federation reluctance and excuses.
corrections.action: Replaced “battle-damaged” with the supported interior evidence and specified the ongoing delays.
